content: The only engine that diverges here is libreoffice, which records a blank (null) cell for every case. This is a recording artifact, not a semantic result: the entire libreoffice fixture for the statistical and statistical-descriptive suites is all-null (0 numeric results across every case, generatedAt 2026-05-11), whereas all other engine fixtures were regenerated later (excel 2026-06-17). The other seven engines (excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc, lattice, pycel) agree on the value for each of these cases. The libreoffice recording needs to be re-run before its blanks can be read as engine behavior.

_meta.evidence: recorded fixtures: fixtures/statistical{,-descriptive}/libreoffice.json are 100% null (0 numeric results), generatedAt 2026-05-11, older than all sibling fixtures

content: These functions are absent from pycel's built-in library, so pycel returns #NAME? (name-resolution failure). Every engine that implements the function agrees on the value up to floating-point display precision (e.g. GEOMEAN(1..5) = 2.605171084697352, HARMEAN(1..5) = 2.18978102189781, STDEV.P(1..5) = 1.4142135623730951, STDEV.S(1..5) = 1.5811388300841898; recorded variants differ only in how many decimals each engine serializes). libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact). Live-confirmed on pure engines: pycel returns #NAME? for GEOMEAN, HARMEAN, STDEV.P, STDEV.S, STDEVA, STDEVPA, VARA, VARPA; hyperformula and ironcalc compute all of these over ranges (the *A family's inline-literal-boolean quirks are a separate case covered by the *A-inline-boolean annotation).

_meta.evidence: live probe (scratch/stat-core-probe1.mts): pycel -> #NAME? for all; hyperformula/ironcalc compute matching values

content: The legacy no-dot names STDEV (sample) and STDEVP (population) are absent from both ironcalc and pycel, which return #NAME?. Both engines DO implement the modern dotted equivalents STDEV.S and STDEV.P (confirmed live: ironcalc computes STDEV.S(1..5)=1.58113883 and STDEV.P(1..5)=1.414213562 but returns #NAME? for STDEV/STDEVP). excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula and lattice implement the legacy aliases and agree (STDEV(1,3)=1.4142135623730951, STDEV(A1:A5 of 1..5)=1.5811388300841898). libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact). This is a naming/alias-coverage gap: the Excel-2010 dotted forms are implemented, the pre-2010 aliases are not.

_meta.evidence: live probe: ironcalc/pycel -> #NAME? for STDEV & STDEVP, but ironcalc computes STDEV.S/STDEV.P

content: This fork turns on how each engine classifies a spreadsheet cell holding a zero-length string "" (empty string), which the corpus seeds via grid values. COUNTA(B1:B3) with B3="" and COUNTA(A1:A3) with A2="": excel, formulas and lattice treat the "" cell as empty and return 2; gsheets, hyperformula and ironcalc treat it as a present text value and return 3. COUNTBLANK(A1:A5) with A2="" (A4,A5 truly empty) mirrors this: excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc and lattice count "" as blank -> 3, while hyperformula counts "" as non-blank -> 2. hyperformula is internally consistent ("" is always a value: counted by COUNTA, excluded by COUNTBLANK); the excel/formulas branch is the opposite ("" is blank: excluded by COUNTA, counted by COUNTBLANK); ironcalc/gsheets count "" for both. pycel returns #NAME? (COUNTA and COUNTBLANK are absent from its library). libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact). Live-confirmed: hyperformula COUNTA=3 / COUNTBLANK=2, ironcalc COUNTA=3 / COUNTBLANK=3, formulas COUNTA=2 / COUNTBLANK=3. Note there is a seeding component: the split also depends on whether the harness materializes "" as a truly-empty cell or an empty-string-valued cell in each engine (see probe request stat-core-001).

_meta.evidence: live probe reproduced the 2-vs-3 (COUNTA) and 2-vs-3 (COUNTBLANK) splits on hyperformula/ironcalc/formulas; excel/gsheets/lattice from recorded fixtures

content: For the *A variance/standard-deviation functions with an inline literal boolean argument (=STDEVA(1,2,TRUE), =STDEVPA(1,2,TRUE), =VARA(1,2,TRUE), =VARPA(1,2,TRUE)), three branches arise from two distinct mechanisms. (1) excel, formulas, gsheets and lattice coerce the inline TRUE to 1 and compute over {1,2,1} -> STDEVA=0.5773502691896258, STDEVPA=0.4714045207910317, VARA=0.3333333333333335, VARPA=0.2222222222222222. (2) ironcalc implements the functions but IGNORES the inline literal boolean, computing over the numeric args {1,2} only -> STDEVA=0.707106781, STDEVPA=0.5, VARA=0.5, VARPA=0.25 (each is exactly the two-element {1,2} statistic). (3) hyperformula and pycel both return #NAME?, but for different reasons: pycel does not implement the *A functions at all, whereas hyperformula DOES implement them over ranges and over inline-numeric args -- it fails here because it resolves the bare keyword TRUE as an undefined name rather than a boolean literal (confirmed live: =SUM(1,2,TRUE) and =AVERAGE(1,2,TRUE) also return #NAME? on hyperformula, while =STDEVA(1,2,3) and =STDEVA(C1:C5) with a boolean in a cell both compute). ironcalc, by contrast, coerces booleans that live in RANGE cells (STDEVA(C1:C5) over {1,text,true,false,2} agrees with the majority at 0.836660027) and coerces the inline TRUE in AVERAGE/AVERAGEA -- so ironcalc's omission is specific to the inline-literal-boolean path of the *A variance/stdev family. libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact).

_meta.evidence: live probe (scratch/stat-core-probe1.mts): ironcalc inline-bool 0.707/0.5/0.5/0.25 vs majority 0.577/0.471/0.333/0.222; ironcalc range-form and AVERAGEA agree

content: =AVERAGEA(1,2,TRUE) forks two ways plus the libreoffice artifact. excel, formulas, gsheets, ironcalc and lattice coerce the inline boolean TRUE to 1 and average {1,2,1} -> 1.3333333333333333. hyperformula and pycel both return #NAME? for different reasons: pycel does not implement AVERAGEA, whereas hyperformula DOES implement AVERAGEA over ranges (=AVERAGEA(C1:C5) over {1,text,true,false,2} -> 0.8, confirmed live) and over inline-numeric args (=AVERAGEA(1,2,3) -> 2) -- it fails on this case because it resolves the bare keyword TRUE as an undefined name rather than a boolean literal (=SUM(1,2,TRUE) and =AVERAGE(1,2,TRUE) likewise return #NAME? on hyperformula). Note ironcalc coerces the inline TRUE here (1.333, agreeing with excel) but IGNORES it in STDEVA/STDEVPA/VARA/VARPA -- see the *A-inline-boolean annotation. libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact).

_meta.evidence: live probe: hyperformula/pycel #NAME?, ironcalc 1.333333333 (agrees with excel/formulas/gsheets/lattice)

content: MODE.MULT is a dynamic-array function (returns all modes as a vertical spill). Three mechanisms appear. (1) hyperformula, ironcalc and pycel do not implement MODE.MULT and return #NAME?. (2) The formulas engine computes the modes but serializes the result array as a STRING literal rather than spilling it: MODE.MULT(1,2,2,3,4) -> "[2]" and MODE.MULT(B1:B5={1,2,2,3,3}) -> "[2, 3]" (an array-handling/rendering artifact of the formulas engine, not a numeric disagreement). (3) excel, gsheets and lattice spill a real array: a single cell 2 for one mode, or a 2-row array [2;3] for the tied dataset. When no value repeats (=MODE.MULT(1,2,3)) excel, formulas, gsheets and lattice all return #N/A (no mode exists) while hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel still return #NAME? (function absent). libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact). Live-confirmed on pure engines.

_meta.evidence: live probe: formulas returns string "[2]"/"[2, 3]"; hyperformula/ironcalc/pycel #NAME?; formulas no-repeats returns #N/A

content: =PERCENTRANK.EXC(A1:A5, 1) over {1,2,3,4,5} forks on both implementation coverage and rounding of the same true value 1/6 = 0.16667. hyperformula, ironcalc and pycel do not implement PERCENTRANK.EXC and return #NAME?. Among implementers, excel and formulas truncate to the default 3 significant digits -> 0.166, while gsheets and lattice round to 3 significant digits -> 0.167. Live-confirmed: formulas returns 0.166 (matching the excel truncation branch). libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact). The number vs number split (0.166 vs 0.167) is a precision/rounding-convention difference in how the 3-significant-digit default is applied, not a difference in the underlying computation.

_meta.evidence: live probe: formulas 0.166 (excel branch); gsheets/lattice 0.167 from recorded fixtures; truncate-vs-round hypothesis needs excel confirmation (stat-core-002)

content: =MAX(-3,-1,-7) and =MIN(-3,-1,-7) expose a pycel parsing limitation: pycel returns #NAME? when MAX/MIN receive inline NEGATIVE numeric literals, even though it evaluates the same functions correctly over positive inline literals (=MAX(1,5,3,2,4)=5) and over cell ranges (=MAX(A1:A3)=30). Live-confirmed on pycel: max-inline-neg and min-inline-neg -> #NAME? while max-inline-pos and max-grid succeed -- so the failure is triggered specifically by the unary-minus literal in an inline argument list, a pycel formula-parser edge, not a missing MAX/MIN implementation. excel, formulas, gsheets, hyperformula, ironcalc and lattice all compute MAX(-3,-1,-7)=-1 and MIN(-3,-1,-7)=-7. libreoffice records blank (all-null fixture artifact).

_meta.evidence: live probe: pycel MAX/MIN inline-negative -> #NAME?; pycel inline-positive and grid forms succeed (isolates unary-minus parse)
